response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT archstat, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM scanqc GROUP BY archstat), s AS (SELECT archstat, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT archstat, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT archstat, cnt AS record_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_above_average FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Missing status means archstat IS NULL. GROUP BY puts NULLs in a single group, which counts as its own status and is included in the average share.
'How far above the average' is the absolute difference, share minus average share. It is not a ratio.
Each row in scanqc is one QC record, so COUNT(*) gives the count per status.
